**Summary of analysis:**

The test image shows very young corn seedlings (V1-V3 stage) in dry/cracked soil. Key features:
- **Overall pale yellowish-green coloration** — significantly lighter than healthy dark-green seedlings
- **Middle plant has brownish/dark staining at the stem base**
- Plants appear somewhat stunted and pale

Narrowing down candidates based on what affects seedlings this early:
- **Downy mildew**: "Infected seedlings are pale yellow or have light-colored striping or mottling on leaves" — strong match; the reference image also showed pale young plants in a field setting at a similar growth stage
- **Stewarts wilt** (seedling phase): pale green to yellow coloration near emergence — possible, but reference images showed slightly more advanced plants with clearer streaking
- All leaf spot, stalk rot, and ear rot diseases of mature plants were eliminated

The pale yellow-green overall coloration of these very early-stage seedlings is the hallmark of Downy mildew infection, which characteristically infects at emergence when soil moisture is high. No other class in this list so explicitly describes pale/yellow young seedlings at this growth stage.
